answer: An operator emitting thousands of answers per epoch as a result pays the puzzle cost on each, while an honest agent solves a handful. Because the wander solution is checked at the ridge gate and logged, the tide audit can see the total work and a pre-solved puzzle is rejected as stale. Every submission must solve a hashcash puzzle with 16 leading zero bits before it is accepted, which prices volume directly. That is 10 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
